stories.title: P&C soft market deepens, but profitability cushion will gradually erode: Swiss Re
stories.summary: Swiss Re has forecast that global non-life insurance premium growth will accelerate over the next two years, even as the P&C and reinsurance market continues to soften. Its Institute's sigma report sees real premium growth of 1.0% in 2027 and 2.0% in 2028, from a 0.5% base in 2026, with growth shifting from pricing-led to exposure-led. Non-life insurer return-on-equity is forecast to fall from 12.7% in 2026 to 10.3% in 2027, and then towards a cost of capital of approximately 7.3% over the medium term.
stories.why_it_matters: Capital built up from recent profits is pushing prices down, so underwriting margins and returns are expected to shrink towards the cost of capital.

stories.title: Supercede expands reinsurance technology partnerships with Inigo and Ascot
stories.summary: Reinsurance technology provider Supercede has agreed deals with Lloyd's insurer Inigo and specialty re/insurance group Ascot to use its Placement Intelligence platform. The London-based company announced both agreements on 17 November 2026, and they let the two firms manage parts of their ceded reinsurance programmes, including broker communications, placement information and market engagement. Inigo has committed to a three-year partnership following a trial, and Supercede already works with companies including Hiscox, Convex, QBE, Allianz and Generali.
stories.why_it_matters: Carriers are investing in data tools to run multi-line, multi-broker reinsurance buying more consistently, and Supercede's client list is growing across the London market.

stories.title: London-listed Nvidia investors slide ahead of crunch results
stories.summary: London-listed technology trusts fell again on Tuesday morning ahead of Nvidia's first results since Jensen Huang's departure. Nvidia's share price sank 4.1 per cent in pre-market trading to $156.1 (£118.3), having plunged as much as 13 per cent last week, and the stock has fallen 32 per cent from its October peak. Polar Capital Technology Trust fell 2.1 per cent to 547.9p and is down 13.9 per cent through the month, while Allianz Technology Trust shed 1.4 per cent and Manchester & London Investment Trust slipped 1.1 per cent.
stories.why_it_matters: Heavy Nvidia holdings, from 9.5 per cent to 12.9 per cent in the largest trusts named, mean one stock's turmoil is feeding straight into UK-listed technology trust prices.

stories.title: Nvidia faces ‘complete evaporation of confidence’ as board rules out Huang return
stories.summary: Nvidia shares slipped further on Tuesday ahead of its third-quarter earnings, as analysts warned of a "complete evaporation of confidence" without a clear stabilisation plan. The stock closed 4.1 per cent lower at $156.14 on Monday and fell a further 0.5 per cent in pre-market trading, extending a sell-off that has wiped roughly $2 trillion from its valuation since October. Wall Street expects revenue of approximately $109bn, up around 90 per cent year on year, while Reuters reported the board is not considering bringing back Huang and is focused on finding a permanent successor.
stories.why_it_matters: Strong demand may no longer be enough to support the share price, as leadership uncertainty and tighter US export restrictions shift the focus to guidance, margins and succession.

stories.title: December interest rate rise ‘difficult to avoid’ after employment jump
stories.summary: UK unemployment fell to 4.6 per cent in the three months to September, the lowest rate since April 2025, according to the Office for National Statistics. Full-time employment rose by 22,000 month-on-month, while pay growth excluding bonuses slowed to 3.5 per cent from 3.7 per cent the previous month. Economists say a second consecutive Bank of England rate rise in December will be "difficult to avoid", and traders have added to bets on it, while vacancies fell a further 22,000 to 690,000.
stories.why_it_matters: Stronger jobs data and pay growth above the 2 per cent target make a further rate rise more likely, which would affect gilt yields, mortgage costs and sterling.
stories.access_note: UK retail investors can get exposure to rate expectations through gilts held directly, bond ETFs, sterling FX, futures, options, and spread bets and CFDs.

stories.title: U.S. Natural Gas Futures Extend Retreat
Zelenskyy gives details on Ukraine’s Crimea bridge operation
stories.summary: Ukraine destroyed part of the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Crimea in a carefully planned operation using Ukrainian weapons, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday. The Russia-installed governor of Crimea, Sergei Aksenov, confirmed the strike and said the bridge was closed until further notice, while the Russian transport ministry said limited traffic will resume on a single railway track. The road portion has collapsed, the damage to the parallel rail bridge is uncertain, and Ukraine says the strike answers a Russian bombing campaign against Ukrainian bridges that began on Oct. 1.
stories.why_it_matters: The $3.7 billion bridge is a key supply line for Crimea's 2.5 million people and Russian forces there, so losing it pushes Russia onto ferries and overland routes that Kyiv can attack.

stories.title: Trump kicks off Asia tour ahead of major talks with Putin, Xi in China
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump flew into Manila for a Quad meeting. He will then travel to China for a much anticipated meeting with his Russian and Chinese counterparts. No further details of the agenda are given.
stories.why_it_matters: A meeting of the US, Russian and Chinese leaders could shape trade, security and sanctions policy, so markets will watch for any signals from it.

market_idea.title: Expressing a view on a second Bank of England hike
market_idea.what_the_trade_is: The view is that a stronger jobs market, with unemployment at 4.6 per cent and pay growth of 3.5 per cent, could lead the Bank of England to raise rates again in December. Traders have already added to bets on this, so the idea is about whether the move is fully priced.
market_idea.how_it_is_expressed: One structure is an outright position in short-dated gilt yields rising, which means gilt prices falling. Another is a position on sterling strengthening against a currency whose central bank is less likely to raise rates.
market_idea.retail_access: A UK retail investor could use short-dated gilt ETFs, gilts held directly, sterling FX pairs, or spread bets and CFDs on gilt futures or sterling. Spread bets and CFDs use leverage and margin, so losses can exceed the initial stake, while gilts held directly are generally free of capital gains tax.
market_idea.what_makes_it_work: The Bank of England has to raise rates in December by more than markets have already priced in, or signal further tightening.
market_idea.what_breaks_it: Weaker data, such as the continued fall in vacancies, could lead the Bank to hold rates and cause the market to reverse its rate-rise bets.
market_idea.disclaimer: An explanation of a trade in the news, not a recommendation.
